about: Every diagnostic of the compiler: the codes of crates/nuclear-diag and their documentation in spec/diagnostics.md.

rows.title: N0001 — reserved word used as a name
rows.summary: Reserved word used as a name
body: **What it is.** Reserved word used as a name
**Why.** Reserved words of the base language (if, for, use, match...) cannot be names.
keys: reserved word used as a name

rows.title: N0002 — tab in indentation
rows.summary: Tab in the indentation
body: **What it is.** Tab in the indentation
**Why.** NuclearLang indents with exactly 2 spaces; tabs are not allowed.

rows.title: N0004 — indentation does not match any block
rows.summary: The indentation returns to no open block
body: **What it is.** The indentation returns to no open block
**Why.** When a block ends, the line must return to the indentation of an enclosing block.
**Example.** a line at 2 when the blocks are at 0 and 4
**Seen with.** A block closed with `}` or a line pasted from another language: fix `N0022` on the lines above first; the indentation errors usually go with it.
keys: indentation does not match any block

rows.title: N0005 — indentation is not a multiple of 2
rows.summary: Indentation that is not a multiple of 2
body: **What it is.** Indentation that is not a multiple of 2
**Why.** Each indentation level is exactly 2 spaces.
keys: indentation is not a multiple of 2

rows.title: N0006 — unexpected character
rows.summary: Unexpected character
body: **Why.** This character is not part of NuclearLang syntax.
**Seen with.** `#` is a comment of another language (`//` in Nuclear); `&` alone is not an operator.

rows.title: N0007 — unterminated string
rows.summary: Unclosed string
body: **Why.** A "..." or '...' string must close on the same line; use """...""" or '''...''' for multi-line text.
**Fix.** close it on the same line, or use `"""`

rows.title: N0008 — unmatched bracket
rows.summary: Unmatched parenthesis, bracket or brace
body: **What it is.** Unmatched parenthesis, bracket or brace
**Why.** Every ( [ { must be closed by its matching ) ] }.

rows.title: N0009 — syntax from another language
rows.summary: Syntax of another language
body: **What it is.** Syntax of another language
**Right.** `and`, `or`, `not x`, `==`, `!=`, and no `;` at the end of a line.

rows.title: N0010 — invalid interpolation
rows.summary: Invalid interpolation
body: **Why.** Interpolation is written "${expr}" with a non-empty expression and a closing }.

rows.title: N0011 — invalid escape sequence
rows.summary: Invalid escape sequence
body: **Tip.** A regular expression is a raw string: `r"\d+"` needs no escapes.

rows.title: N0012 — invalid number
rows.summary: Invalid number
body: **Why.** Numbers are 42, 1_000, 3.14 or 0xff, with no letters after them.

rows.title: N0013 — unexpected token
rows.summary: Unexpected token
body: **Why.** The parser expected a different token here; see the message for what was expected.
**Fix.** the message says what was expected

**Most common cause.** A decorator written after the field or method it belongs to, or on the same line: the message is `'@column' has no member below it`. A decorator goes on the line right above its member:

rows.title: N0014 — range followed by a method needs parentheses
rows.summary: Range followed by a method without parentheses
body: **What it is.** Range followed by a method without parentheses
keys: range followed by a method needs parentheses

rows.title: N0015 — typed lambda parameter without a block
rows.summary: Typed lambda parameter without a block
body: **What it is.** Typed lambda parameter without a block
**Why.** list.map(x: T) declares lambda parameters, so the call must be followed by an indented block. For a one-line lambda write list.map((x: T) => expr).
keys: typed lambda parameter without a block

rows.title: N0016 — function declared inside a body
rows.summary: Function declared inside a body
body: **What it is.** Function declared inside a body
**Why.** Functions cannot be declared inside another function. Assign an anonymous function: name = (params) Type, followed by its block.
**Example.** `helper(x: int) int` + block inside a function

rows.title: N0017 — statement in a module body
rows.summary: Statement in the body of a module
body: **What it is.** Statement in the body of a module
**Why.** A module body holds fields (name: Type = value), methods and the constructor. Code that runs on construction goes in the constructor block: (params) followed by an indented block.
**Fix.** field `localAttr: string = "x"` or assign it in the constructor
**Right.** Inside a module (a class, a kind) only fields and methods: `count: int = 0` is a field; an assignment belongs inside a method.

rows.title: N0018 — module declared inside a module
rows.summary: Module declared inside another module
body: **What it is.** Module declared inside another module
**Why.** Modules are declared at the top level of a file.
**Fix.** declare it at the top level

rows.title: N0019 — invalid assignment target
rows.summary: Invalid assignment target
body: **Why.** Only names, $fields, members (a.b) and indexes (a[i]) can be assigned.
**Example.** `f() = 1`; `pieces = ~pieces(raw)` inside a module with a method `pieces` (a method is not a variable)
**Fix.** a name, `$field`, `a.b` or `a[i]`; another name for the variable
**Seen with.** A local variable named like a method of its own module (`pieces = ~pieces(raw)`): give the variable another name (`planned = ~pieces(raw)`).

rows.title: N0020 — one-line function returning void
rows.summary: One-line function returning void
body: **What it is.** One-line function returning void
**Why.** A function that returns void must be written with an indented block.

rows.title: N0021 — comment line without ` * `
rows.summary: Comment line without ` * `
body: **Why.** Each line that continues a `//` comment starts with ` * `: the `*` goes right under the second `/` of the `//`.
**Fix.** ` * text`, with the `*` below the second `/` (the fix writes it)

rows.title: N0022 — habit of another language
rows.summary: Habit of another language (TypeScript, Dart, Python, Java, Go); the other errors of that line are not shown
body: **What it is.** Habit of another language (TypeScript, Dart, Python, Java, Go); the other errors of that line are not shown

**Why.** A form of TypeScript, Dart, Python or Java (`{ }` blocks, `await`, `const x =`, `new`, `class`, `def`, `elif`, `None`, `#` comments, the return type first). The message gives the NuclearLang form and, when it is exact, a fix.
**Example.** `f() int {`, `await g()`, `const x = 1`, `new User()`, `class A extends B`, `int f(int x)`, `def f(self):`, `elif`, `None`, `# note`, `i++`, `import { a } from "x"`
**Fix.** the NuclearLang form; the fix writes it when it is exact (`f() int`, `~g()`, `x = 1`, `User()`, `A: B`, `f(x: int) int`, `else if`, `null`, `// note`, `i += 1`, `use x{ a }`)
**Fix it first.** The compiler hides the other errors of a line that has a habit, because they only repeat the same mistake. `nuclear fix` applies the exact ones.
// no braces, no semicolons, no const, no new, no await, no return on the last line
Each habit has its row: `habit:` (search the word you wrote: `await`, `const`, `new`, `import`, `class`, `switch`).

rows.title: N0102 — duplicate declaration
rows.summary: Duplicate declaration
body: **Why.** Two declarations in the same file produce the same name.

**Example.** two `User` in the same file; a member declared twice in one module (`load()` twice); a call to a method hidden by a local of the same name (`prompt(...)` inside `write(prompt: string)` of a module with a method `prompt`)
**Seen with.** A small model that writes the same method twice, or copies into its file a declaration another file already has: write only what the task declares.

rows.title: N0103 — if/match inside an expression needs one expression per branch
rows.summary: `if`/`match` with multi-line branches inside an expression
body: **What it is.** `if`/`match` with multi-line branches inside an expression
**Why.** Branches of several lines are allowed when the if/match is the value of an assignment or of a return; inside a larger expression every branch must be a single expression.
**Right.** Give the branch a variable first: `label = if a` + its branches, then `f(label)`.
keys: if/match inside an expression needs one expression per branch

rows.title: N0104 — invalid enum item
rows.summary: Invalid enum item
body: **Why.** An enum block only holds items written as name or name(value).
**Example.** an enum that mixes `user` with `name: string`

rows.title: N0105 — name used outside the block that created it
rows.summary: Name used outside the block that created it
body: **What it is.** Name used outside the block that created it
**Why.** A variable created inside a block (if, for, while, match, try) exists only in that block. To take a value out of an if or match, use it as a value: x = if cond ...
**Example.** `text` created inside an `if` and read after it
**Right.** Create the variable before the block and assign it inside, or make the `if` the value: `text = if ok` + branches.
keys: name used outside the block that created it

rows.title: N0106 — undefined name
rows.summary: Undefined name
body: **Why.** The name is not a variable, parameter, member, declaration or import of this file.
**Example.** `page` not declared, not a parameter nor an import

**Check, in this order.** A typo; a variable created inside an `if` or `for` and read after it (`N0105`); a parameter the method does not have; a name of the target's library the dialect does not know (`nuclear defs search <text>`); a declaration of another file that the task forgot to list.

rows.title: N0107 — destructuring pattern mixes new and existing names
rows.summary: Pattern mixing new and existing names
body: **What it is.** Pattern mixing new and existing names
**Why.** A pattern either declares new variables or assigns existing ones: [a, b] = xs with a and b both new, or both already declared.
**Example.** `[a, b] = xs` with `a` already declared and `b` new
keys: destructuring pattern mixes new and existing names

rows.title: N0108 — result that can fail is not handled
rows.summary: Unhandled `Result` outside a function that returns `Result`
body: **What it is.** Unhandled `Result` outside a function that returns `Result`

**Why.** A call that returns Result<E, T> propagates its error automatically only inside a function that also returns a Result. Elsewhere, handle it with match (Ok(x) -> ... / Err(e) -> ...), keep it in a variable typed Result<T, E>, or declare the function's return type as Result<T, E>.
**Example.** `user = findUser(id)` in a function that returns `string`

**Right.** Either make the function return a `Result` (then `user = findUser(id)` unwraps it and an `Err` leaves by itself), or handle both cases: `match findUser(id)` + `Ok(user) -> ...` / `Err(e) -> ...`.
keys: result that can fail is not handled

rows.title: N0109 — propagated error has another type
rows.summary: The propagated error has another type
body: **What it is.** The propagated error has another type
**Why.** An error propagates only to a function whose Result has the same error type. Convert it first: call(x).error(e => Err(MyError(e))).
**Example.** `findUser` fails with `string` and the function returns `Result<AppError, Order>` (fix: `findUser(id).error(e => Err(AppError(e)))`)

rows.title: N0110 — result cannot propagate from this position
rows.summary: A `Result` that cannot be propagated from that position
body: **What it is.** A `Result` that cannot be propagated from that position

**Why.** A Result is unwrapped before its statement runs. Inside a branch that may not run (the right side of and, or, ??, a ternary, an else if or while condition, an if in a list) assign it to a variable first.
**Example.** `ok and findUser(id).active` (fix: assign it to a variable first)
keys: result cannot propagate from this position

rows.title: N0111 — invalid use of a Result
rows.summary: Invalid use of a `Result`
body: **What it is.** Invalid use of a `Result`

**Why.** A match on a Result has arms Ok(name) ->, Err(name) -> and _ ->, one pattern per arm. A callback of .ok()/.error() returns Ok(...)/Err(...) in every branch (it transforms) or in none (it only observes). An async function gives its Result with ~: match ~load(id).
**Example.** a branch `Ok(1) ->` in a `match`; an `.error()` callback that returns `Ok(...)` only in some branches; `match load(id)` with an async `load` (missing `~`)

rows.title: N0112 — alias of a method that cannot be reached
rows.summary: Alias of a method that cannot be reached
body: **What it is.** Alias of a method that cannot be reached
**Why.** name() = Module.method makes name the same function as method. A method that is not static is called on a new Module(), so every constructor parameter of Module needs a default.
**Example.** `find() = Repo.find` with `Repo(url: string)`: the alias creates a new `Repo()` and `url` has no default (fix: give it a default, or write `find` as a method)
keys: alias of a method that cannot be reached

rows.title: N0113 — top-level statements in a file with main
rows.summary: Top-level statements in a file with `main` (targets that run them in `main`, like Dart)
body: **What it is.** Top-level statements in a file with `main` (targets that run them in `main`, like Dart)
**Why.** In a target where top-level statements run inside main (Dart), a file cannot have both: move the statements into main(). Top-level variables (`limit = 10`) are allowed.
**Example.** `print("hi")` at the top level and `main() void` in the same file (fix: move the statement into `main`; a top-level variable `limit = 10` is allowed)
keys: top-level statements in a file with main

rows.title: N0114 — not a member of Nuclear's standard library
rows.summary: Not a member of Nuclear's standard library (library.md): a target's name on a base type, a function of a target (`len`, `str`, `parseInt`), a static of a target (`Math.floor`, `JSON.stringify`), a property called as a method or a method used as a property
body: **What it is.** Not a member of Nuclear's standard library ([library.md](library.md)): a target's name on a base type, a function of a target (`len`, `str`, `parseInt`), a static of a target (`Math.floor`, `JSON.stringify`), a property called as a method or a method used as a property

**Why.** The members of string, lists, maps, sets, numbers, Bytes, DateTime, Duration, Regex and Match are Nuclear's own (spec/library.md, `nuclear help library`), the same in every dialect: a target's name (push, len, toUpperCase, contains) is replaced by the Nuclear one given in the message.

**Example.** `xs.push(x)` (fix: `add(x)`), `text.toUpperCase()` (fix: `upper()`), `len(xs)` (fix: `xs.length`), `xs.length()` (fix: `length` is a property); a kept `Result` read as its value (`found.length`, `found[0]` in a test: `found.value.length`)
`add` not `push` or `append`; `upper()` not `toUpperCase()`; `length` is a property (no parentheses) and never `len(x)`; membership is `x in xs`, never `contains` or `includes`.
**In a test.** `found.length` on a kept `Result` is this error too: read `found.value.length`.
keys: not a member of nuclear's standard library
asks: how do I get the length of a list

rows.title: N0115 — the receiver's type is not known
rows.summary: The receiver's type is not known and the member is written differently for each base type in this dialect
body: **What it is.** The receiver's type is not known and the member is written differently for each base type in this dialect

**Why.** A member of the standard library is written differently for each base type in this dialect, and the type of the value before the dot is not known: declare it (`items: string[] = ...`, a typed parameter) or build the value from a literal or a typed call.

**Example.** `items.length` where `items` comes from a value without a type (fix: declare it, `items: string[] = ...`); only in the dialects where the bases differ (TypeScript's `length` against `size`)
keys: the receiver's type is not known

rows.title: N0116 — unknown member of a declaration of the project
rows.summary: A member that a declaration of the project does not have: the value's type is a model, class or kind whose members are all known (its own, its project bases' and those of the runtime classes it or its kind inherits when the type definitions list them; the kind's `method_members`), and the message names them as the `.nuc` writes them
body: **What it is.** A member that a declaration of the project does not have: the value's type is a model, class or kind whose members are all known (its own, its project bases' and those of the runtime classes it or its kind inherits when the type definitions list them; the kind's `method_members`), and the message names them as the `.nuc` writes them

**Why.** The value's type is a declaration of this project whose members are all known (its fields, methods and constructor parameters, its project bases, and the runtime classes it or its kind inherits when the type definitions list their members), and it has no member with that name. A model generated from a contract changes when the backend changes: rebuild and read the generated file.

**Example.** `saved.done` when `Task` has `completed` (a contract the backend changed); `~loans.get(id)` on a repository (the runtime's is `find`); the message names the closest member and all of them
**Fix.** rebuild (a contract) or fix the name

**Check.** The message lists every member the declaration has: use one of them. A repository's own methods are `find`, `findAll`, `save`, `remove`; a model of a contract changed when the backend changed (build the backend, or `nuclear contracts update`).
keys: unknown member of a declaration of the project

rows.title: N0201 — unknown header word for the dialect
rows.summary: Header word unknown to the dialect
body: **What it is.** Header word unknown to the dialect
**Why.** Words before a declaration's name must be kinds or modifiers defined by the active dialect (dialect files: [kinds.*], [modifiers.*]).

**Check.** The word before the name must be a kind of the project's platform (`nuclear help words --platform

`): `usecase`, not `use case`; `appcomponent`, not `component` on the backend; a kind of the mobile platform does not exist on the backend.
keys: unknown header word for the dialect

rows.title: N0202 — unknown clause for the dialect
rows.summary: Clause unknown to the dialect
body: **What it is.** Clause unknown to the dialect
**Why.** Words after a declaration's name (on String, with Flyer) must be clauses defined by the active dialect ([clauses.*]).
**Example.** `Bird: Animal with Flyer` with the `typescript` dialect

rows.title: N0203 — the dialect does not define a template
rows.summary: The dialect does not define a template
body: **What it is.** The dialect does not define a template
**Why.** The active dialect (or the dialect it extends) has no [syntax] template for this construct.
keys: the dialect does not define a template

rows.title: N0204 — shortcut collision
rows.summary: Shortcut collision
body: **Why.** Two shortcuts, kinds or auto-imports define the same name. Each name must be defined once across a dialect and the dialects it extends; to replace a parent entry, list it in [dialect] replaces.

rows.title: N0205 — shortcut very similar to another
rows.summary: Shortcut very similar to another (warning)
body: **What it is.** Shortcut very similar to another (warning)
**Why.** Two shortcut names differ by one character or only by case, which invites typos.

rows.title: N0206 — invalid dialect file
rows.summary: Invalid dialect file
body: **Why.** The dialect file is not valid TOML, has a value of the wrong type, or a template with invalid syntax.
**Example.** malformed TOML, a value of the wrong type, a template with an unclosed `{{#x}}`

rows.title: N0207 — dialect not found
rows.summary: Dialect not found or circular inheritance
body: **What it is.** Dialect not found or circular inheritance
**Why.** No dialect with that name was found in the dialect search path, or `extends` forms a cycle.
**Example.** `--dialect rubi`, `a extends b` and `b extends a`

rows.title: N0208 — the target allows a single base
rows.summary: The target allows only one base
body: **What it is.** The target allows only one base
**Why.** The target language of this dialect supports extending only one base.
**Example.** `Admin: User, Person` in TypeScript or Dart
keys: the target allows a single base

rows.title: N0209 — kind requires a member
rows.summary: The kind requires a member
body: **What it is.** The kind requires a member
**Why.** This dialect kind requires a member (for example stateless requires build).

rows.title: N0210 — unknown template variable
rows.summary: Unknown variable in a template (warning)
body: **What it is.** Unknown variable in a template (warning)
**Why.** A dialect template uses a variable that the transpiler does not provide for that template.

rows.title: N0211 — unknown use clause
rows.summary: Unknown `use` clause
body: **Why.** Words after a use path (show, hide, deferred) must be listed in the dialect's [use] clauses.

rows.title: N0212 — shortcut named like a base keyword
rows.summary: Shortcut named like a reserved word
body: **What it is.** Shortcut named like a reserved word
**Why.** Shortcut names cannot be reserved words of the base language.
keys: shortcut named like a base keyword

rows.title: N0213 — type definitions package not found
rows.summary: Type definitions package not found or invalid
body: **What it is.** Type definitions package not found or invalid

**Why.** A package of [dialect] defs (name@version) or one of its depends is not in the definitions repository (--defs-path, $NUCLEAR_DEFS_PATH, the defs/ folder next to each dialects/ folder), or its files are invalid. Generate it with tools/defs.
**Example.** `defs = ["flutter@9.9.9"]` without that version in the `defs/` repository

rows.title: N0214 — two versions of the same type definitions package
rows.summary: Two versions of the same definitions package
body: **What it is.** Two versions of the same definitions package
**Why.** A dialect and the dialects it extends (or the depends of their packages) ask for two versions of the same definitions package. Use one version.
**Example.** `dart` asks for `dart@3.13.5` and a child dialect for `dart@3.12.0`
keys: two versions of the same type definitions package

rows.title: N0215 — method not allowed in this kind
rows.summary: Method not allowed in the kind
body: **What it is.** Method not allowed in the kind
**Why.** The kind declares the only methods it can have ([kinds.<k>] methods); a usecase has a single exec method.
**Example.** a second method in a `usecase` (only `exec` is allowed)
**Right.** One use case, one operation: a second operation is a second `usecase` file. A helper several use cases share is a `service`.
keys: method not allowed in this kind

rows.title: N0216 — the kind requires another return type
rows.summary: The kind requires another return type
body: **What it is.** The kind requires another return type
**Why.** Every method of this kind must return the type its dialect names ([kinds.<k>] returns), for example Result<E, T> in a usecase.
**Example.** `exec() Character` in a `usecase` (it must return `Result<E, T>`)
keys: the kind requires another return type

rows.title: N0217 — unknown or missing argument of a decorator
rows.summary: Unknown or missing decorator argument (`[decorators.args]`)
body: **What it is.** Unknown or missing decorator argument (`[decorators.args]`)
**Why.** The dialect lists the arguments of the decorator ([decorators.args]): each named argument, each field of an object argument, and the ones that are required (!).

**Check.** The message lists the arguments the decorator has. Look it up: `nuclear help --platform

`.
keys: unknown or missing argument of a decorator

rows.title: N0218 — the kind does not write that part of the declaration
rows.summary: The kind does not write the declaration's generics (`<T>`) or interfaces (`> I`): they would be lost
body: **What it is.** The kind does not write the declaration's generics (`<T>`) or interfaces (`> I`): they would be lost

**Why.** The template of the kind never writes the generics (<T>) or the interfaces (> I) of the declaration, so they would be lost: remove them or use a kind (or a plain declaration) that writes them.
**Example.** `Page<T>` with a kind whose template does not use `generics`; `@stateModel(S) statemanager M > Comparable`
keys: the kind does not write that part of the declaration

rows.title: N0219 — named argument the constructor does not have
rows.summary: Named argument the constructor does not have (from the type definitions; files of a project)
body: **What it is.** Named argument the constructor does not have (from the type definitions; files of a project)
**Why.** The type definitions list the parameters of the constructor; the message names the closest one and all of them. `nuclear defs show <Class> --dialect <d>` prints the constructor.
**Fix.** the closest parameter (`style`); the message lists all of them
keys: named argument the constructor does not have

rows.title: N0220 — unknown class
rows.summary: PascalCase call that nothing defines (files of a project, dialects with type definitions); also a call's type argument (`inject<Missing>()`), not a generic parameter
body: **What it is.** PascalCase call that nothing defines (files of a project, dialects with type definitions); also a call's type argument (`inject<Missing>()`), not a generic parameter
**Why.** A PascalCase call that is not declared in the project, imported, nor in the dialect's type definitions. `nuclear defs search <text> --dialect <d>` finds the real name.
**Fix.** the closest known name (`Column`); `nuclear defs search`

**Check.** A typo in a class of a library (the message gives the closest one); or a class of the project that no file declares: `inject<BooksAppComponent>()` needs a file that declares `appcomponent BooksAppComponent`. In a run of the Loop this means the plan missed a piece.

rows.title: N0221 — a method of this kind needs a body
rows.summary: A method of the kind needs a body
body: **What it is.** A method of the kind needs a body

**Why.** The kind's methods do something ([kinds.<k>] needs_body): an appcomponent method is an alias of a use case (`find() = GetOne.exec`) or has a body. A method without one would be generated empty.
**Example.** `booksOf(author: string) Result<Error, Book[]>` alone in an `appcomponent` (it would be generated empty)
**Fix.** an alias `booksOf() = BooksOfAuthor.exec`, or a body
**Right.** An application component is only aliases to use cases:
keys: a method of this kind needs a body

rows.title: N0222 — an asynchronous call used without `~`
rows.summary: An asynchronous call used without `~`
body: **What it is.** An asynchronous call used without `~`
**Why.** A member or an index of what an asynchronous call returns (`books.exec(a).length`) reads a value that is not there yet: await the call, `(~books.exec(a)).length`.
**Example.** `expect(booksOfAuthor.exec("Ada").length > 0)` (the length of a promise); `found = books.all()` then `found.length` (the variable holds the call)
**Right.** Await once, keep the value, then use it:
Every call to a repository, a use case, an `appcomponent` alias, an agent or a model is asynchronous. `nuclear fix` adds the `~`.
asks: how do I await a call

rows.title: N0301 — architecture: this declaration cannot use that one
rows.summary: A declaration uses another one its kind does not allow (`[architecture] callers`), or a name its kind cannot use (`[architecture] names`)
body: **What it is.** A declaration uses another one its kind does not allow (`[architecture] callers`), or a name its kind cannot use (`[architecture] names`)

**Why.** The dialect's [architecture] callers says which kinds can use each kind (a usecase only from an appcomponent, a service only from a usecase or an aggregate), and [architecture] names which kinds can use a name (BuildContext only in views).
**Example.** a screen calls a `usecase` (only an `appcomponent` calls it); a `statemanager` receives a `BuildContext`

**The allowed calls.** Backend: controller → `appcomponent` → use case → repository, service or aggregate. Mobile and web: screen → state manager → `appcomponent` → use case → repository or service. Only views use the build context and navigate.
It is not a typo: move the call to the kind that may make it, and add the alias to the facade.
keys: architecture: this declaration cannot use that one
asks: why can't my controller call a repository
who can call a use case

rows.title: N0302 — architecture: private to its component
rows.summary: A declaration uses something private of another component (`[architecture] public`)
body: **What it is.** A declaration uses something private of another component (`[architecture] public`)
**Why.** Only the kinds listed in [architecture] public (the appcomponent) are visible from other components; use the component through its appcomponent.
**Right.** Depend on the other component's `appcomponent` (`characters: CharactersAppComponent`), and add there the alias you need.

rows.title: N0303 — invalid project
rows.summary: Invalid project
body: **Why.** The project has no nuclear.toml, the manifest is invalid (config.nuc: only its sections, with named literal values), or two files declare the same name.
**Example.** `nuclear.toml` is missing, two files declare the same name, or the manifest in Nuclear (`config.nuc`) has another section, an unnamed argument or a value that is not a literal

rows.title: N0304 — a plugin the project has not enabled
rows.summary: A kind or a name of a plugin the project does not enable (`[project.plugins]` of the dialect)
body: **What it is.** A kind or a name of a plugin the project does not enable (`[project.plugins]` of the dialect)

**Why.** The kind or the name belongs to an optional plugin of the dialect (Genkit, Kafka, LangChain...). A project carries a plugin only when its config.nuc enables it: plugins(name = true). The message gives the exact line.
**Right.** The message says the line. In `config.nuc`:
plugins(sqlite = true, ai = true, ollama = true)
keys: a plugin the project has not enabled
asks: why is agent not a kind

rows.title: N0305 — a dialect does not match its platform
rows.summary: A dialect does not match its platform's contract (`dialects/<platform>/platform.toml`, ADR-0093): a kind missing or added, a consumed decorator or a plugin the platform does not declare (a plugin the dialect does not bring yet is a warning)
body: **What it is.** A dialect does not match its platform's contract (`dialects/<platform>/platform.toml`, ADR-0093): a kind missing or added, a consumed decorator or a plugin the platform does not declare (a plugin the dialect does not bring yet is a warning)

**Why.** A dialect in dialects/<platform>/ must implement that platform's contract (platform.toml, ADR-0093): the same kinds, and no consumed decorator or plugin the platform does not declare, so the Nuclear of a project never changes with its dialect. A platform plugin the dialect does not bring yet is a warning.
**Fix.** declare it in `platform.toml` and implement it in every dialect of the platform, or drop it
keys: a dialect does not match its platform

rows.title: N0306 — kind package without an implementation for the dialect
rows.summary: A kind package (`kinds/<name>/`, ADR-0095) enabled in `config.nuc` has no implementation for the project's dialect
body: **What it is.** A kind package (`kinds/<name>/`, ADR-0095) enabled in `config.nuc` has no implementation for the project's dialect

**Why.** A package of extension kinds (kinds/<name>/, ADR-0095) implements some dialects of its platform; enabling it in config.nuc ties the project to those dialects. Build with one of them, or add a folder for this dialect to the package.
**Example.** `plugins(jobs = true)` with `kinds/jobs/fastapi/` only, built with `nestjs` (fix: build with fastapi, or add `kinds/jobs/nestjs/`)
keys: kind package without an implementation for the dialect

rows.title: N0307 — contract not available
rows.summary: A contract the manifest declares (`contracts(name = "../path" | "https://...")`, ADR-0098) cannot be read: the backend at that path was never built, a url contract was never fetched, or the JSON is invalid
body: **What it is.** A contract the manifest declares (`contracts(name = "../path" | "https://...")`, ADR-0098) cannot be read: the backend at that path was never built, a url contract was never fetched, or the JSON is invalid

**Why.** The manifest declares a contract (contracts(name = "../path" | "https://...")) that cannot be read: build the backend project at that path first, or fetch a url contract with `nuclear contracts update` (it keeps a copy in contracts/<name>/contract.json).
**Fix.** build the backend (`nuclear build ../tasks_api`) or run `nuclear contracts update`

rows.title: N0308 — a field decorator's rule is not met
rows.summary: A field decorator's rule is not met (`[decorators.fields]` of the platform, ADR-0100): a relation field is optional, its type is an entity (a list for `@oneToMany`/`@manyToMany`), `@manyToOne` needs its column `<name>Id`, `inverse` names a field of the related entity, one side of a `@manyToMany` has `@joinTable` and one side of a `@oneToOne` has `@joinColumn`
body: **What it is.** A field decorator's rule is not met (`[decorators.fields]` of the platform, ADR-0100): a relation field is optional, its type is an entity (a list for `@oneToMany`/`@manyToMany`), `@manyToOne` needs its column `<name>Id`, `inverse` names a field of the related entity, one side of a `@manyToMany` has `@joinTable` and one side of a `@oneToOne` has `@joinColumn`

**Why.** A decorator of a field has rules of its platform ([decorators.fields] of platform.toml): the field is optional, its type is a list or not, its type is a declaration with a decorator (an @entity), a sibling field exists (`projectId` for `@manyToOne project`), an argument names a field of the field's type (`inverse`). The message says which rule and the fix.
**Right.** A relation field is optional, its type is an entity, and a `@manyToOne` keeps its column in a field of its own:
keys: a field decorator's rule is not met

rows.title: N0309 — not a decorator of the platform
rows.summary: A project of a platform writes a decorator in lower case its platform does not declare (`decorators` of `platform.toml`): the dialect would drop it or write it as something else. The message names the closest one, or what replaced a removed one (`[decorators.replaced]`)
body: **What it is.** A project of a platform writes a decorator in lower case its platform does not declare (`decorators` of `platform.toml`): the dialect would drop it or write it as something else. The message names the closest one, or what replaced a removed one (`[decorators.replaced]`)

**Why.** A project of a platform (backend, mobile, web) writes only the decorators its platform declares (`decorators` of platform.toml): one that is not there would be dropped or written as something else by the dialect. The message names the closest one, or what replaced a removed decorator (`@generated` → `@primary(generated = true)`, ADR-0100). Decorators in PascalCase (a converter, a target's own decorator) are not checked.

**Check.** The decorators of a platform: `nuclear help words --platform

`. `@generated()` is now `@primary(generated = true)`.
keys: not a decorator of the platform
